name: equal
algorithm: Compare two equal-length buffers for equality, a one-bit difference planted at random within the last 64 bytes in about half the reps and removed after each compare; the checksum is total * 31 + equal over the reps, wrapping (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: no integer arithmetic to wrap in the kernel: the checksum already wraps

skip.mk: std.simd dispatches at run time (simd.Cpu()), so on an avx2 machine the Mk column runs its 32-lane form (on an AVX-512 machine its 64-lane avx512bw form, D-353); this fixed-v2 variant would compare it with 16-byte vectors. Mk is compared in the v3 variants (status/std-simd.md, request R-3)

std.simd dispatches at run time (simd.Cpu()), so on an avx2 machine the Mk column runs its 32-lane form (on an AVX-512 machine its 64-lane avx512bw form, D-353); this fixed-v2 variant would compare it with 16-byte vectors. Mk is compared in the v3 variants (status/std-simd.md, request R-3)

std.simd dispatches at run time (simd.Cpu()), so on an avx2 machine the Mk column runs its 32-lane form (on an AVX-512 machine its 64-lane avx512bw form, D-353); this fixed-v2 variant would compare it with 16-byte vectors. Mk is compared in the v3 variants (status/std-simd.md, request R-3)

no_counts: B24 does not apply as a count of operations: each compare reads both buffers to the planted difference in the last 64 bytes, and the checksum folds every result in order
notes: On a CPU with AVX-512 (the owner's Ryzen 7 9800X3D has it) the mk column of the v3 variants runs std.simd's 64-lane `cpu "avx512bw"` form from 256 bytes up (D-353), while c, rust and zig are fixed at x86-64-v3: the Mk cell is then not at the same width. bench-final labels it or adds a v4 variant (status/bench.md, from std-simd).

GB/s counts 2 * size * reps bytes: each compare reads both buffers (the difference, when planted, is in the last 64 bytes). The fill and its first-touch page faults are timed by each variant's baseline (reps 0) and subtracted (BS-3). The c, rust, zig and go buffers start on a 64-byte boundary (BS-4); the mk column reads arena slices whose alignment Mk code cannot set without std.raw (BS-4's labelled exception, tests/bench/README.md).

c: <immintrin.h>, four XORs ORed and tested with _mm*_testz_si* a step (glibc's __memcmpeq shape, std.simd.Equal's method), chosen by __AVX2__. rust: the same with std::arch, every load from a checked slice (BS-2). zig: @Vector XORs reduced with @reduce(.Or). go: bytes.Equal, assembly-backed in Go's runtime with its own CPU check, labelled. mk: std.simd.Equal.

Checksums from the go column (go run testdata/equal.go at each size, 2026-11-07). The repetitions were estimated from the count row's single-run rates for about 1 s of the c cell at L1 and L3 (std-simd session 2, 2026-11-07).
